tagline: Four paved miles on the island across the harbor.
intro: Chappaquiddick starts with a short crossing. From Edgartown a barge-like ferry carries walkers, bicycles and up to three cars at a time over to the island, and Chappaquiddick Road takes it from there, four paved miles across an island of red cedar woods, salt marsh and salty ponds. Off the pavement, sandy woodland roads and trails go on to the shore.

The name comes from a word for separated island, though a narrow barrier beach has tied it to Martha's Vineyard for most of modern history, between storms. Longtime residents speak of going to the mainland when they cross to Edgartown, and of going to America when they head for Boston.

moments.title: Edgartown
moments.text: Whaling captains lined Water Street with houses topped by widow's walks, which were handier for pouring sand down a burning chimney than for watching for sails.

moments.title: Mytoi
moments.text: A small Japanese garden in an open pine forest, where an arched footbridge crosses to an island in a little pond.

moments.title: Cape Poge Light
moments.text: The 1893 tower at the island's northeast tip has been moved four times, the last time by helicopter, and stands a 3.5-mile walk from Dike Bridge.
